title: Login and Session Management
summary: Explains authentication, role-driven access, session behavior, and practical troubleshooting.

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: RAPTOR performs server-validated session checks during active use. Unsaved edits can be lost when re-authentication is required.

sections.title: Authentication contract
paragraphs: Authentication and authorization are enforced separately. The RAPTOR login form posts to `/login`; Flask validates credentials with Keycloak (direct grant) and then establishes a server-side session. Enabled OIDC/SAML connections add Sign in with … buttons that start `/auth/sso/{alias}/start` and return through `/auth/sso/callback`. The browser keeps the HttpOnly Flask cookie; Keycloak access and refresh tokens stay on the server. Route visibility and actions still use role plus effective permissions from the identity cache.
After login, RAPTOR loads session status and applies capability checks before rendering module navigation and page actions.

sections.title: First access and reset behavior
paragraphs: Some accounts are provisioned with Keycloak required action `UPDATE_PASSWORD`. RAPTOR maps that to `password_reset_required` and routes users through password reset before granting a normal session. LDAP and other federated users authenticate with their directory password; incomplete Keycloak profile required actions are cleared on login instead of sending those users into password reset.
This prevents partial operational access under transitional credential state.

sections.title: Session lifecycle
paragraphs: RAPTOR tracks session validity continuously. A warning dialog appears before expiration and offers explicit continuation or logout paths.

rows: Warning dialog with `Stay logged in (+1h)` and `Log out`.
User confirms continuation or session termination.

sections.title: Logout semantics
paragraphs: Logout requests server-side session termination and always clears client-side auth state. Even when network failure occurs, local state is invalidated as a safety fallback.

sections.title: Troubleshooting pattern
paragraphs: Most access issues are caused by expired sessions, missing permissions, or reset-required account state. Validate these conditions first before deeper diagnostics.

rows: Session expiration or cookie policy mismatch.
Re-authenticate and validate browser cookie settings.
Permission not granted to current account.
Compare role and optional permissions with expected profile.
Complete reset flow or confirm user policy with admin.
